newsitem.title: USA: British nanny held without bail in infant's death.
newsitem.headline: British nanny held without bail in infant's death.

text.p: An 18-year-old British nanny pleaded not guilty on Thursday and was ordered held without bail on a charge of murder in connection with a 9-month-old boy's death from head injuries.

Louise Woodward, who arrived in the United States in June from her home in Chester, England, is accused of fatally injuring Matthew Eappen in a moment of frustration. The baby was rushed to a Boston hospital on Feb. 4 and hospital officials said it died late on Sunday from head injuries.
Woodward began working for the infant's parents, Deborah Eappen, 31, an opthalmologist, and Sunil, 30, an anaesthesiologist, in November.
Police in Newton, a Boston suburb, said she told them she had handled the baby roughly in the bathroom and later shook him when she was frustrated by his fussiness.
Woodward showed no emotion during the hearing. Her father Gary and British consular officials were in the courtroom and left immediately without talking to reporters.

"We have no intention of trying this case in the media but feel it is necessary to stress that Ms. Woodward has pleaded not guilty to the charges against her involving Matthew Eappen, and we are confident that a full airing of the facts will prove she bears no responsibility for this tragedy," her lawyers said in a statement released after the hearing.

"She is absolutely no threat to the community or the victim's family," defence lawyer Maria Galvagna argued in an unsuccessful effort to get her client's $100,000 bail reduced. Instead, Newton District Court Judge Conrad Beletzer ordered Woodward held in custody after entering her not guilty plea.
Her lawyers were expected to appeal the ruling.
Neither of the child's parents was in the courtroom. They have another son, Brendan, 2.

Prosecutor Lynn Rooney told the judge a preliminary autopsy showed Matthew had suffered a skull fracture. "The amount of force applied to this child was extremely severe. In addition to the shaking, the child was struck on a flat surface object," she said.
Rooney said the severity of the murder charge will be decided by a grand jury, which is expected to hear the case and hand up a formal indictment in the next few weeks.
